'''Paul Snowdell Russell Jr.''' (January 22, 1925 – August 22, 2026) was an American physician.

== Early life and career ==
Russell was born in [[Chicago]], Illinois on January 22, 1925, the son of Paul S. Russell Sr., a [[banker]] and a former [[college football]] [[quarterback]], and Carroll Mason, a [[Investor|financial banker]] for dancer [[Martha Graham]].<ref name="a" /> He attended [[Groton School]].<ref name="c" /> He attended the [[University of Chicago]], earning his [[Bachelor of Arts|BA degree]] in [[philosophy]] in 1944, his [[Bachelor of Science|BS degree]] in [[chemistry]] in 1945 and his [[Doctor of Medicine|MD degree]] in 1947. After earning his degrees, he worked at [[Massachusetts General Hospital]], and served in the [[United States Air Force]] during the [[Korean War]], which after earning his discharge, he completed his residency in [[Massachusetts]] in 1956<ref name="a">{{Cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/02/obituaries/paul-russell-dead.html|title=Paul S. Russell, an Innovator in Transplant Medicine, Dies at 101|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=September 2, 2026|access-date=September 11, 2026|first=Trip|last=Gabriel}}</ref>

He taught at [[Columbia University College of Physicians and Surgeons|Columbia College of Physicians and Surgeons]] in New York for two years, and he served as a professor in the department of [[surgery]] at [[Harvard Medical School]] (HMS). During his years as a professor at HMS, in 1964, he was elected as a member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.amacad.org/person/paul-snowden-russell|title=Paul Snowden Russell|work=[[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]|access-date=September 11, 2026}}</ref> and from 1988 to 2021, he served as chair and vice chair of the Joint Committee of the [[Boston Medical Library|Countway Library]].<ref name="c" /> In 1998, he was named the [[John Homans]] [[Distinguished professor|Distinguished Professor]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://hms.harvard.edu/about-hms/office-dean/messages/honoring-paul-russell|title=Honoring Paul Russell|work=[[Harvard Medical School]]|date=August 28, 2026|access-date=September 11, 2026}}</ref>

In 2004, Russell was awarded the Medawar Prize by the Transplantation Society.<ref name="c" />

== Personal life and death ==
In 1952, Russell married Allene Lummis. They had four children. Their marriage lasted until her death in 2010.<ref name="a" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/houstonchronicle/name/allene-russell-obituary?id=23492219|title=Allen Russell Obituary (2010)|work=[[Houston Chronicle]]|date=March 28, 2010|access-date=September 11, 2026|via=[[Legacy.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/bostonglobe/name/paul-russell-obituary?id=62381811|title=Paul Russell Obituary (1925-2026)|work=[[The Boston Globe]]|date=September 9, 2026|access-date=September 11, 2026|via=[[Legacy.com]]}}</ref>

Russell died at his home in [[Westwood, Massachusetts]], on August 22, 2026, at the age of 101. According to his ''Dignity Memorial'' obituary, he was named a "legendary figure" by [[George Q. Daley]], the dean of HMS.<ref name="c">{{Cite web|url=https://www.dignitymemorial.com/obituaries/boston-ma/paul-russell-13012698|title=Paul Snowden Russell Jr.|work=Dignity Memorial|access-date=September 11, 2026}}</ref>
